scope: A frozen 338-ID detector-gap definition review. Pending designs are not executable rules and do not count toward capacity.
source_attribution: Technique names and definition excerpts: MITRE ATT&CK, https://attack.mitre.org/resources/terms-of-use/ . Design notes and rules: GTISC MalwareLab.
admission_policy: A current official definition and a discriminating predicate are required for every enabled rule.
Static feature co-occurrence is a capability candidate; successful dynamic matches are observation candidates.
A rule may cover one concrete implementation of a technique without covering every variant.
Do not derive ATT&CK IDs from tactic keywords, generic API names, malware-family labels, or automatic parent roll-up.
Pending definitions, synthetic fixtures, and declared telemetry requirements never create sample evidence.
No runtime or completion credit without separate sample/caller/target/effect qualification.

techniques.name: Data Obfuscation
techniques.official_definition_excerpt: Adversaries may obfuscate command and control traffic to make it more difficult to detect.[1] Command and control (C2) communications are hidden (but not necessarily encrypted) in an attempt to make the content more difficult to discover or decipher and to make the communication less conspicuous and hide commands from being seen.
techniques.definition_requirement: Require a reconstructed C2 message and a decoder/encoder relationship showing concealment, rather than simply a network send.
required_observables: process-bound network endpoints and transport
protocol/payload or removable-medium content
relationship of transferred bytes to the C2, collected-data, relay, or exfiltration role in the definition
techniques.reason_deferred: Connection, DNS, cryptography, or file-transfer API names do not establish the channel role or content transformation required by this technique.
